description: Same 4 tasks against the site's own documented public API (https://automationexercise.com/api_list), which the site publishes precisely so it can be automated against -- no reverse-engineering or undocumented endpoint use.

RT1.notes: POST /api/searchProduct search_product=dress -- correct, 9 results, matches DOM exactly.

RT2.notes: GET /api/productsList (one call), then filtered the response locally for category.usertype=='Women' && category.category=='Dress'. Correct: same 3 products as DOM.

RT3.notes: Answered from the SAME productsList response already fetched for RT2 -- filtered locally for brand=='Polo'. Zero additional HTTP calls. Correct: same 6 Polo products as DOM.

RT4.notes: Also answered from the same cached productsList response by looking up id==1. Correct: Blue Top, Rs. 500, Polo -- matches DOM exactly.

finding: One GET /api/productsList response contains brand and category metadata for every product, so it alone answers RT2, RT3, and RT4. The DOM product-listing page does not surface brand/category as visible text on the listing view -- that information only becomes visible per-product-detail-page or per-category-page, which is why the DOM agent had to make 3 separate navigations for what the API answered from 1 cached response.
